title: Check yourself: what each stand-in can catch

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A gateway forwards purchases from many terminals under one terminal ID. Its tests drive the forwarding code from eight threads at once against a FakeMux, and all of them pass. In production the log fills with Duplicate key errors. Why did the tests show nothing?

options.text: The fake compares no keys, so it answered two requests that had one key
options.says: only a real QMUX builds keys and refuses a second request with the key of one still waiting; a fake answers whatever it is given

options.text: The tests used too few threads, so their STANs never collided at one moment
options.says: no number of threads helps against a fake: it never compares keys, so it answers colliding requests like any others

options.text: The fake renumbers each STAN, so it never received two requests with one key
options.says: a fake changes nothing in the request; it answered colliding requests because it never compares keys

options.text: The tests used no real host, so nobody was there to report the repeated STAN
options.says: QMUX raises Duplicate key itself, before sending; no host is involved in it

origin.section: 10.2 A Fake Checks Your Decisions, and Only QMUX Checks jPOS's Rules

questions.stem: To save time, a team starts the client's Q2 once from a script before Maven runs, and the integration tests call QMUX.getMUX("host-mux") to reach it. What do those tests get?

options.text: The running QMUX, since getMUX reaches it through the host and port named in its descriptor
options.says: getMUX opens no connection; it reads the NameRegistrar of the JVM it runs in

options.text: A NotFoundException, since the registry that getMUX reads exists only in the JVM that runs Q2
options.says: the NameRegistrar is a static map per JVM, so Q2 has to run inside the test's JVM

options.text: The running QMUX, since Q2 publishes each deployed component for other processes to look up
options.says: the lookup reads the in-process NameRegistrar; nothing another process deployed is in it

options.text: A NotFoundException, since getMUX finds a MUX only after the test itself has called q2.ready
options.says: q2.ready only waits for a deployment; the lookup fails because the QMUX lives in another JVM's registry

origin.section: 10.3 Only a Test That Deploys Your Files Tests Them

questions.stem: An embedded test calls q2.ready() with a generous timeout, then calls authorize on unit c4's client right away. The host stand-in was started before Q2. On the build server the test sometimes gets HOST_UNAVAILABLE. Which change stops that?

options.text: Add a two-second sleep after ready(), so the link has time to come up first
options.says: a sleep is right only by accident; a first connect that fails waits a whole reconnect-delay, ten seconds by default

options.text: Wait for the QMUX in the NameRegistrar, so the purchase goes out once it is there
options.says: ready() returns after the deployment, so the QMUX is already registered; what may be missing is the link

options.text: Add a longer timeout to ready(), so Q2 has time to deploy every file first
options.says: ready() already returned true; the files were deployed, and the timeout changes nothing about the connection

options.text: Wait for the ready entry in the Space, so the purchase goes out once it is there
options.says: ready() means deployed, not connected; a blocking rd on host-channel.ready returns as soon as the link is up

origin.section: 10.4 A Test Waits for a Condition, Never for a Time

questions.stem: A new merchant's city is one character longer than its field allows. The client is tested only against a FakeMux. Where does the problem first show?

options.text: In the fake-MUX tests, since the fake packs each message before it answers it
options.says: a fake MUX never packs; it answers the ISOMsg object it was handed

options.text: In production, in the calling thread, since QMUX packs each request before it queues it
options.says: QMUX queues the ISOMsg; the adaptor's sender thread packs it when it writes to the socket

options.text: In the fake-MUX tests, since ISOMsg.set checks each value against its field
options.says: an ISOMsg holds strings and checks nothing; only the packager knows the field's length

options.text: In production, on the adaptor's thread, since the channel packs each message as it sends it
options.says: nothing packs the message before the adaptor's sender thread does, so without a round trip through the link's packager the first failure drops the link

concepts: Descriptors, channel and packager are tested only by running Q2 in the test's JVM on the shipped files against a host on 127.0.0.1, because the NameRegistrar is per JVM.

A fake MUX checks the client's decisions but not QMUX's rules: missing key fields, duplicate keys and unmatched answers show up only with a real QMUX, which can run in the test against a host on its queues.
A round trip through the link's packager finds a field that doesn't fit in the build, where otherwise it first fails on the adaptor's thread.
